native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE period occurred in the 15th century BCE (1500–1401 BCE), continuing into the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE): the mean KDE growth rate (g_all_mean) peaks at +0.00283 in 1500–1401 BCE (rank 1 of 9 full century bins), with all ten fastest growth years falling at 1452–1432 BCE, and the independent pollen-openness growth proxy (pollen_grate_100) also ranks 1500–1401 BCE first (+0.00189), with its fastest years at 1424–1415 BCE. The growth take-off follows centuries of near-zero growth (20th–17th centuries BCE, means −0.00007…+0.00028) and is followed by sustained negative growth in the 13th (−0.00155) and 12th (−0.00438) centuries BCE. Supporting characterization: during the peak bin, weapon (hatchets/swords), hoard, axe/celt, amber and monument-count Z-indicators are above the window mean, and landscape openness rises from its window minimum (15th century) to its maximum (14th century). Limitation: annual series are interpolated from sparse inputs (raw Z at century marks only; raw pollen n=177), so exact peak timing may partly reflect interpolation artifacts, although two independent proxies and bin-offset sensitivity (~1450–1400 BCE) agree.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500) and pollen openness CSV (decimal=','), restricted to CE −2000…−1100 (901 rows). 2) Binned into BCE centuries using label(CE)=100*ceil(−CE/100) (Nth century BCE = CE −N…−(N−100)+1); merged the single-row CE −1100 endpoint into the 1200-BCE bin. 3) Computed mean/median/max of g_all_mean and pollen_grate_100 per century with ranks (century_table.csv). 4) Robustness: median-vs-mean ranks (Spearman 1.0) and ±50-year bin-edge offsets (peak stays in 1500/1400 BCE bins, underlying interval ~1450–1400 BCE). 5) Used openness levels (pollen_inter_100, SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) and interpolated Z-indicators only as supporting characterization of what was growing. Artifacts: analysis/growth_phase_analysis.py (executed), analysis/century_table.csv.
